correctness.rationale: For d>=2 and a>=1, polarity gives K°=B_2^d intersect {|y1|<=1/a}. With t=1/a, integrate the polar sections to 2 kappa_(d-1) I_d(t). The meridian of K has sphere radius sqrt(1-z²) until z=t and tangent conical radius (1-tz)/sqrt(1-t²) from t to1/t. Integrating yields primal volume 2 kappa_(d-1)[I_d(t)+(1-t²)^((d+1)/2)/(dt)]; hence exact Mahler product. Differentiation of I(I+H) and integration by parts gives derivative proportional to f(t)[I-(d+2)J/(d t²)], J=int_0^t s²f(s)ds, f(s)=(1-s²)^((d-1)/2). Strict reversed Chebyshev inequality J<t² I/3 implies derivative >2(d-1)fI/(3d)>0 for every 0<t<1, so the product strictly decreases with a. Endpoint a=1 gives kappa_d², a->infinity gives unattained 4kappa_(d-1)²/d; Taylor gives next (d-1)/(3a²). d=3 simplifies to exact quartic 4pi²(3+2/a²-a^-4)/9. Independent Simpson meridian integrations d=2,3,4,8 at a=1,1.2,2,5,20 corroborated strict decay. Finite quadrature is not the all-dimensional proof.
